rows.question: Before the Abortion Legislation Act of 2020, what were the legal conditions and time limits for abortion in New Zealand under the previous law (the Contraception, Sterilisation, and Abortion Act 1977)?
rows.answer: Under the Contraception, Sterilisation, and Abortion Act 1977, abortion in New Zealand was technically a criminal offense under the Crimes Act 1961, but could be legally performed if two certifying consultants agreed that specific grounds were met. These grounds included serious danger to the life or physical or mental health of the pregnant woman, substantial risk of serious physical or mental disability of the fetus, and pregnancy resulting from incest or sexual violation. For pregnancies up to 20 weeks, these standard grounds applied. After 20 weeks gestation, abortion was only permitted in cases of serious danger to the woman's life or risk of serious permanent injury to her physical or mental health. The two-certifying-consultant requirement made the process more restrictive in practice than in many comparable countries.
